The client will only pay when milestones are achieved, so if there is any delay in development, the company will have no money to pay the bank back and can default.
Another issue is that the company has limited assets to give as security and no previous experience with projects of this size. Banks will either refuse the loan or charge a very high interest rate because of this risk. Also, I noticed the plan depends a lot on the government grant, which is not even confirmed yet. It is not wise to take a big loan hoping that a grant might get approved later.
So In my opinion, a better option would be to ask the client for some advance payment, or take a smaller loan, or maybe let an investor buy a small share of the company. Losing a little ownership is much better than losing the whole company because of debt.

Answer: No.

In my opinion, the CEO's decision to obtain a large bank loan is not justified under the given circumstances because it creates significant financial risks for the newly established company. The project requires substantial initial investment, while the client will release payments only after completing specific milestones. This may create cash flow problems if project activities are delayed or milestones are not achieved on time.

Furthermore, the company has limited assets to provide as security and no previous experience in managing projects of this size. Repaying a large loan with interest could become difficult if client payments are delayed. Depending on an uncertain government grant is also risky because its approval may take time or may not be granted at all.

Instead, the CEO should explore safer financing options, such as applying for the government grant, negotiating advance payments or partial milestone payments with the client, and obtaining a smaller loan if necessary. The company should also prepare a realistic financial plan before starting development.

Therefore, taking a large bank loan without guaranteed financial support or a reliable repayment plan could threaten the company's financial stability. Retaining full ownership is important, but financial sustainability should be the first priority.
